subject: botany_2
question_text: Give one example each of a transgenic plant suitable for food processing and one with improved nutritional quality.

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.46, printed question 123. insider_note: Two names, one line each. Flavr Savr and golden rice — both need the property that makes them the answer.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Food processing
steps.margin_note: The variety, the crop, and the property. Four lines.
lines: Transgenic plant suitable for food processing:
the FLAVR SAVR variety of TOMATO.
Its ripening is DELAYED, so it is bruise resistant
steps.why: Delayed ripening is exactly what a food-processing crop needs: time between harvest and use.
common_mistakes: Naming golden rice here. Golden rice is the NUTRITION example.
Giving the name with no property. Delayed ripening is why it qualifies.
steps.memory_tip: Flavr Savr ripens slowly, so it travels well.

steps.label: Nutritional quality
steps.margin_note: The variety, the compound, and what it prevents.

lines.text: Flavr Savr for processing; golden rice for

lines: Transgenic plant with improved nutritional value:
GOLDEN RICE, from the Taipei rice variety.
It is rich in beta-carotene, which the body turns
into VITAMIN A, and so helps prevent blindness.
steps.why: Rice grain carries no beta-carotene naturally, so adding it changes the nutritional value of the staple food itself.
common_mistakes: Saying golden rice is bruise resistant. That is Flavr Savr.
Saying it contains vitamin A. It contains BETA-CAROTENE, the precursor.
steps.memory_tip: Golden from the carotene, and carotene becomes vitamin A.
